key_insight: This paper introduces a motion-conditioned, multi-view fusion approach to localize myocardial infarction from echocardiography more effectively than methods that rely on handcrafted motion features or dense annotations. By leveraging motion cues across multiple echo views, it aims to identify damaged heart regions with less supervision.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of detecting and localizing myocardial infarction from echocardiography when strong annotation is limited. The paper tackles the gap between clinically important regional wall motion abnormalities and AI methods that are either annotation-hungry or not well suited to multi-view echo data.
method: Uses motion-conditioned learning to capture regional wall motion abnormalities directly from echocardiography.
Fuses information across multiple echocardiographic views to improve localization robustness and reduce ambiguity from single-view analysis.
Builds on foundation-model-style visual representations to avoid reliance on handcrafted motion descriptors and dense manual supervision.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how to combine motion modeling with multi-view fusion for a clinically meaningful classification/localization task under weak supervision. The approach is relevant to medical imaging settings where labels are scarce but anatomy and motion across views provide complementary evidence.

paper_title: Motion-Conditioned Multi-View Fusion for Myocardial Infarction Localization from Echocardiography
paper_authors: Guang Yang, Wentian Xu, Siyu Wang, Betty Raman, Lei Li
